papers.title: Melatonin-loaded proniosomes enhance gemcitabine response in gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma: Proteomic and computational insights.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM) remains a major barrier in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) therapy. Melatonin has multi-targeted antitumor activity but is limited by rapid elimination and low oral bioavailability. We developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) and evaluated its physicochemical properties, ex vivo permeation, and antitumor activity, alone and with GEM, in a GEM-resistant CCA model. MPN was prepared by a provesicular slurry method and characterized for physicochemical properties, stability, molecular dynamics (MD), and ex vivo permeation. Efficacy and tole
papers.summary: This study developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) formulation to overcome melatonin's poor bioavailability and tested it, alone and combined with gemcitabine, in a gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma model. MPN improved melatonin delivery and, when combined with gemcitabine, enhanced antitumor response in resistant cells. Proteomic and computational analyses were used to explore the mechanisms underlying the reversal of gemcitabine resistance.

papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a viral mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to uncover new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective as the virus evolves and acquires resistance to existing drugs.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that expands beyond classical PROTACs to include newer targeted protein degradation modalities such as molecular glues and XTACs. It also incorporates AI-powered knowledge discovery features to help researchers mine the growing body of degrader data and support computational design of new degraders.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method using multiple instance learning, which focuses on local functional domains and catalytic residues rather than whole-sequence embeddings. This approach aims to improve Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction without relying on accurate 3D structures, addressing limitations of existing methods. The method is designed to be broadly applicable for protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction.

papers.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA-ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures.
papers.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extra
papers.summary: ARIEL is a new, freely accessible database that manually curates experimentally measured RNA-ligand binding affinities (Kd values) and links them to the corresponding 3D structures from the Protein Data Bank. By screening nearly 7,000 RNA-containing structures, it addresses a critical bottleneck in RNA-targeted drug discovery: the lack of paired affinity and structural data needed to train and validate computational models. This resource should accelerate rational design of small molecules that bind RNA.

papers.title: Harnessing engineered laccase and functional carrier materials for efficient dye degradation: From mechanism to application.
papers.abstract: Laccases are copper-containing oxidases that have been widely investigated for the decolorization and degradation of synthetic dyes, including azo, anthraquinone, triphenylmethane, indigo and thiazine dyes. However, their application in dye-containing wastewater remains constrained by enzyme instability under complex effluent conditions, limited oxidation of some recalcitrant or high-redox-potential dyes, mediator dependence, and poor recovery and reuse of free laccase. This review discusses recent progress in laccase-catalyzed dye degradation from a mechanism-to-engineering perspective, linki
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in using laccase enzymes, combined with engineered carrier materials, to degrade synthetic dyes in wastewater. It connects the catalytic mechanisms of laccase with engineering strategies aimed at overcoming enzyme instability, limited substrate range, mediator dependence, and poor reusability. The work frames laccase-based dye remediation as a mechanism-to-application pipeline.

papers.title: Wrapping mechanism of β-lactoglobulin around SDS micelles characterized by time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Conformational transitions of water-soluble proteins at membrane interfaces play an important role in biological functions and diseases. Herein, we present a novel analytical framework capable of revealing the unique stepwise wrapping of β-lactoglobulin (bLG) around anionic sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) micelles by integrating time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism (TR-VUVCD) spectroscopy with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. TR-VUVCD spectra of bLG interacting with SDS micelles were measured over 0.4-90 s, revealing that this interaction induces a β-to-α conformational transit
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: This study combines time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism spectroscopy with molecular dynamics simulations to track how β-lactoglobulin wraps around anionic SDS micelles over a 0.4–90 second timescale. The authors observe a stepwise conformational transition from β-sheet to α-helix as the protein engages the micelle surface, revealing a wrapping mechanism relevant to protein–membrane interactions.

papers.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fu
papers.summary: This paper presents an iterative, physics-based computational workflow that simulates directed evolution in silico to engineer enzymes. Unlike generative AI approaches whose decision logic is opaque, this method uses physics-based scoring to propose and evaluate mutations across cycles, aiming to sample protein design space more transparently. The approach offers an interpretable alternative for enzyme engineering.

papers.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m6A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage.
papers.abstract: Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1-3 (YTHDF1-3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged an
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify small-molecule inhibitors that bind the m6A pocket (the YTH aromatic cage) of YTHDF proteins, yielding hits DT11 and DT15 with selectivity for YTHDF2 as well as pan-YTHDF activity. This provides starting chemical scaffolds for probing and potentially drugging m6A reader function, with relevance to cancers such as glioblastoma where YTHDF2 is a dependency.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a recombinant Bacillus laccase (frL103) degrades aflatoxin B1 without requiring a mediator, tracking the reaction over 60 hours. UHPLC-HRMS profiling shows AFB1 declines to ~24% and ~15% of initial levels at 30 and 60 h, while an intermediate feature at m/z 329.0660 rises then falls, indicating a stage-dependent transformation pathway rather than simple depletion. The work highlights that parent-toxin loss alone is an incomplete measure of detoxification and provides structural evidence for intermediate products.

papers.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
papers.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characteriz
papers.summary: This study links bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to urothelial injury resembling ferroptosis and cellular aging, mediated by the lipid-metabolism enzyme ACSL4, and proposes this as a mechanism relevant to Hunner-type interstitial cystitis. In a human cohort, higher urinary BPA was associated with a related phenotype, and experimental work implicates ACSL4 in the BPA-driven injury.

papers.title: On the limits of marginal protein folding stability: methodological goals and drawbacks.
papers.abstract: Why do proteins remain at the edge of stability rather than evolving toward maximal thermodynamic robustness? Can we trust the computational methods that inform about when and how stability falls off that edge? Marginal stability, the confinement of protein folding free energies to a window of approximately 5-15 kcal/mol, is broadly observed in biophysics, and its mechanistic causes, involving evolutionary and biophysical properties, remain under debate and require accurate predictions. In this regard, protein folding stability is currently predicted using both traditional structure-based homo
papers.summary: This paper critically examines why proteins evolve to be only marginally stable (folding free energies of ~5–15 kcal/mol) rather than maximally stable, and evaluates the reliability of computational methods used to predict folding stability. It argues that both evolutionary and biophysical explanations for marginal stability remain debated, and that current structure-based prediction tools have methodological limitations that affect our ability to assess when and how stability is lost.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Relative Ligand Binding Free Energy Simulation Methods: Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug design has become increasingly important in the pharmaceutical industry for accelerating the discovery of effective drug candidates. In particular, ligand binding free energy serves as a critical metric for predicting drug efficacy during the key stages of hit discovery and lead optimization. Continuous progress has been made in the prediction of ligand binding free energies, but direct comparisons of different methods using the same force field remain challenging due to their unique implementations in different simulation engines. In this study, we present a direct compar
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study directly compares four relative ligand binding free energy simulation methods—Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD—using the same force field to isolate methodological differences from implementation effects. The comparison provides a benchmark of accuracy and efficiency across these widely used alchemical free energy approaches, helping guide method selection for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (h
papers.summary: SynBioFooDB is a new database that links food-related compounds to their biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence, addressing the fragmentation of this information across literature and existing food resources. It aims to enable cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems for food compounds.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, built using a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors developed the workflow by systematically evaluating free and template-based docking methods, ligand similarity, and maximum common substructure approaches on an expanded benchmark. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data for machine-learning scoring functions in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: A piperamide natural compound is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2: In silico and in vitro model study.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) is a well-known key regulator of angiogenic cancers. In a structure-based virtual screening of Indonesian natural compounds, dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide from Piper species, emerged as a promising VEGFR2-binding candidate. However, its inhibitory activity against VEGFR2 has not been experimentally validated. This study combined molecular simulations and cellular assays to investigate the potential interaction between DPN and VEGFR2. Molecular docking predicted that DPN occupies the regulatory domain pocket (RDP) spanning the ca
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide natural compound, as a candidate VEGFR2 binder that appears to occupy the regulatory domain pocket and adopt an inactive DFG-out conformation. Molecular simulations and cellular assays were combined to validate the predicted interaction, supporting DPN as a potential anti-angiogenic agent. The work provides experimental support for a natural-product VEGFR2 inhibitor with a distinct binding mode.

papers.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation.
papers.abstract: RNA viruses encode multiple layers of information within a single molecule, which functions simultaneously as a template for protein synthesis and as a structured regulatory RNA. These structures control key aspects of viral gene expression, govern host interactions, and mediate immune evasion. Although the prevalence of RNA structure in viral genomes is now well established, only recently have functional and mechanistic studies begun to uncover how these elements act as regulatory modules that shape infection outcomes. With their compact genomes and experimentally tractable life cycles, RNA v
papers.summary: This review discusses how RNA viruses pack regulatory information into structured RNA elements within their compact genomes, using the same RNA molecule for both protein coding and gene regulation. It highlights recent functional and mechanistic studies showing how these RNA structures control viral gene expression, host interactions, and immune evasion, and argues that viruses are powerful models for understanding structure-based riboregulation.

papers.title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases.
papers.abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a singl
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce gEDES-HM, a computational protocol that uses enhanced sampling simulations of a single protein to map conformational ensembles onto homologous proteins, allowing functional transitions to be predicted across a protein family. They demonstrate the method on adenylate kinases, showing that state distributions and functional behaviors can be inferred for homologues without running separate simulations for each. This offers a scalable way to link conformational landscapes to function across related proteins.

papers.title: Physical determinants of reliable RNA-ligand binding prediction revealed by P-RISE.
papers.abstract: RNA-targeted small-molecule discovery is challenged by the scarcity of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes and by the limited transferability of current computational approaches across chemically diverse systems. Here we present P-RISE, a physics-grounded framework for RNA-ligand binding prediction, and use it to identify the physical determinants underlying reliable performance. Systematic evaluation of force fields, ionic environments, dielectric treatments, and entropy corrections reveals three coupled requirements: preservation of RNA-binding pocket integrity under ion-sensit
papers.summary: The authors introduce P-RISE, a physics-based framework for predicting RNA–ligand binding, and use it to systematically test how force fields, ionic conditions, dielectric treatments, and entropy corrections affect accuracy. They find that reliable prediction requires preserving RNA binding-pocket integrity under ion-sensitive conditions, along with coupled treatment of electrostatics and entropy. The work clarifies which physical modeling choices matter most for RNA-targeted small-molecule discovery.

papers.title: In-silico transcriptomic characterization analysis identifies SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy requiring reproducible biomarkers and structurally tractable therapeutic targets. We applied an integrated transcriptomic, network, virtual-screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular-dynamics (MD) workflow using GSE8671, GSE14333, and GSE89076. Differential expression analysis (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC= ≥ 1) identified 2092 upregulated/9130 downregulated genes in GSE8671, 926/945 in GSE14333, and 2317/1456 in GSE89076. Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from three colorectal cancer datasets with network analysis, virtual screening, docking, ADMET profiling, and molecular dynamics to identify SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as candidate biomarkers and druggable targets. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation, so the proposed biomarkers and targets remain hypotheses requiring wet-lab confirmation.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study develops a three-stage, thermophysically guided framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules with improved thermal stability. Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for preselection of coating materials. The approach aims to reduce probiotic viability losses during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit for food applications.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong adhesion in wet and underwater conditions, where a hydration layer normally blocks adhesive contact. It discusses the synergistic mechanisms of interfacial chemical bonding and multiscale energy dissipation that underlie wet adhesion, and how these biological strategies inspire the design of multifunctional adhesives for complex humid and underwater environments.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins, a family of seven-transmembrane retinal-binding membrane proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi that perform light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. It traces the field from the 1971 discovery of bacteriorhodopsin through the channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics revolution, with particular emphasis on Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins and their potential as optogenetic silencing tools. The paper synthesizes how structural understanding informs the engineering of light-controlled neuronal inhibition.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: The authors designed water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes that mimic enzyme active sites to selectively break down poly(bisphenol A carbonate) plastic under mild alkaline conditions. The optimized nanozyme achieved a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase, and binding studies confirmed strong substrate recognition. This offers a rational design strategy for targeted plastic depolymerization and recycling.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: This study introduces a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship and enable rational design. By combining molecular docking with activity assays, the authors identify key dipeptide modules that influence ACE inhibition, providing a framework for engineering improved antihypertensive peptides for functional foods.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines food-derived umami peptides as natural flavor enhancers that could reduce reliance on salt and conventional seasonings in alternative proteins and cultivated meat. It compares discovery approaches ranging from traditional sensory-guided preparation to modern virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization, emphasizing the need for experimental validation beyond sequence prediction.

papers.title: Structural basis of phospholipid sensing nuclear receptor LRH-1 recognition by carboxylic acid bioisosteres reveals an alternative ligand interaction site.
papers.abstract: Liver receptor homolog-1 (LRH-1; NR5A2) is a phospholipid-sensing nuclear receptor that regulates metabolic and steroidogenic pathways in the liver, intestine, and pancreas. Previously, we showed that small-molecule LRH-1 agonists with carboxylic acid "tails" mimic endogenous phospholipid contacts at the mouth of the ligand-binding pocket, enhancing receptor activation. To improve metabolic stability while preserving these key interactions, we designed a series of agonists in which the carboxylate was replaced with bioisosteric polar groups. Substituting a tetrazole for the carboxylate in a le
papers.summary: The authors designed LRH-1 agonists replacing the carboxylate with bioisosteric polar groups like tetrazole to improve metabolic stability while preserving key phospholipid-mimicking contacts. Structural analysis revealed that these bioisosteres engage an alternative ligand interaction site at the mouth of the ligand-binding pocket, providing a structural basis for phospholipid sensing by this nuclear receptor.

papers.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id
papers.summary: This study combined machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and umbrella sampling to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential inhibitors of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), a cancer drug target. A CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies and narrowed the pool to 26 promising compounds, which were then validated through docking and simulation approaches. The work demonstrates an integrated computational pipeline for prioritizing natural-product drug candidates against ALK.

papers.title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation.
papers.abstract: Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscap
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-scale computational pipeline—docking, missing-loop reconstruction, molecular dynamics in a lipid bilayer, and MM/PBSA free-energy calculations—to characterize how four chemically diverse natural compounds (hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, isoliquiritigenin) bind and modulate the human SGLT2 glucose transporter. The work derives design principles for natural-product modulators of this established type 2 diabetes drug target, highlighting binding modes and energetic determinants that could guide future ligand optimization.

papers.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized a series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrid compounds using click chemistry (CuAAC) and tested them as dual inhibitors of EGFR and CDK1, two kinases important in cancer cell growth. The compounds were screened for antiproliferative activity against four human cancer cell lines, with mechanistic and computational (in silico) studies supporting the dual-target binding hypothesis. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying a new scaffold for potential anticancer development.

papers.title: Whole-proteome structure/function prediction in uropathogenic E. coli reveals previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of high-throughput sequencing technologies has vastly increased the number of known protein sequences, but the experimental characterization of their structures and functions lags behind. This gap in knowledge impedes our understanding of biological mechanisms of these proteins, hinders the interpretation of high-throughput experiments, and exposes a significant challenge in modern biology: deducing the structural and functional information of proteins based on their sequences. Most computational approaches rely on homology with well-annotated proteins, yet many proteins
papers.summary: The authors applied whole-proteome structure and function prediction to uropathogenic E. coli, going beyond homology-based annotation to uncover previously missed host-microbe and microbe-phage interaction pathways. This demonstrates that structure-informed proteome-scale prediction can reveal functional roles for uncharacterized proteins and expand the known interaction landscape of a pathogen.

papers.title: Tomatidine derivatives suppress Dengue virus infection through entry and post-entry inhibition.
papers.abstract: Dengue is a rapidly spreading disease transmitted by mosquitoes and is caused by the Dengue virus (DENV), affecting approximately 390 million individuals globally. Approved vaccines for use have limited efficacy, and there are no approved antivirals. Tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid obtained from Solanum species, has demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral properties, leading to the investigation of its derivatives for their anti-DENV activity. In the current study, the anti-DENV potential of tomatidine and 11 such derivatives was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in silico approaches
papers.summary: This study tested tomatidine, a steroidal alkaloid from Solanum plants, and 11 of its derivatives for activity against Dengue virus using in vitro and computational methods. Several derivatives suppressed DENV infection by blocking both viral entry and post-entry steps. The findings suggest tomatidine derivatives are promising leads for antiviral development against dengue, for which no approved drugs currently exist.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities are being extended beyond structure determination to ligand-target recognition, particularly for natural product research. It highlights applications for complex bioactive molecules like peptides and molecular glues, where limited structural data has historically hindered mechanism elucidation and drug optimization.

papers.title: Atomistic insights into the migration and diffusion behavior of crosslinking byproducts in polyethylene networks.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of crosslinking byproducts, such as cumyl alcohol and acetophenone, in polyethylene (PE) insulation accelerates the degradation of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables through space charge formation and electrical tree propagation. Since conventional degassing processes cannot entirely eliminate these crosslinking byproducts, characterizing their residual dynamic behavior is of paramount importance. This work presents a comprehensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulation study to quantify the diffusion kinetics of these byproducts within the PE network. By systematically var
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how crosslinking byproducts (cumyl alcohol and acetophenone) migrate and diffuse through polyethylene networks used in high-voltage cable insulation. The work characterizes the diffusion kinetics of these residual molecules, which cannot be fully removed by conventional degassing and contribute to cable degradation. The findings provide atomistic insight into byproduct mobility that could inform improved degassing or insulation design strategies.

papers.title: Unrevealed oligoresveratrols from Shorea parvifolia root bark as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: isolation, in vitro bioassay, quantum studies and structure-based computational profiling.
papers.abstract: Resveratrol oligomers from Shorea species possess diverse biological activities, but the structural determinants governing their inhibition of xanthine oxidase (XO) remain poorly understood. This study investigated oligoresveratrols isolated from the root bark of Shorea parvifolia and examined how their structures relate to XO inhibitory potential. Five oligoresveratrols were isolated and structurally characterized by spectroscopic analysis. We evaluated their XO inhibitory activities, followed by pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness predictions, DFT calculations, molecular docking, and molecular
papers.summary: This study isolated five resveratrol oligomers from Shorea parvifolia root bark and tested their ability to inhibit xanthine oxidase, an enzyme target for gout treatment. The authors combined in vitro enzyme assays with computational docking, quantum chemistry calculations, and pharmacokinetic predictions to explore how structural features of these natural compounds relate to inhibitory activity. The work provides a structure-activity framework for oligoresveratrols as potential xanthine oxidase inhibitors.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel indenonaphthodiazepine propellane compound via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized it spectroscopically. DFT calculations probed its electronic properties, and molecular docking against the anti-apoptotic cancer target Mcl-1 gave a binding score of -5.678 kcal/mol, modestly outperforming a comparator. The work is a preliminary computational/chemical study without experimental validation of Mcl-1 inhibition.

papers.title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA.
papers.abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialize
papers.summary: Researchers characterized a PNGaseA-family enzyme from an infant-associated gut bacterium, Bifidobacterium bifidum, that cleaves N-glycans from glycoproteins to release them as nutrients. Structural and biochemical analyses show the enzyme prefers N-glycans attached to glycopeptides over those on intact or denatured proteins, suggesting it is specialized for processing partially digested milk glycoproteins in the infant colon.

papers.title: Full-fat soybean origin and thermal processing affect protein secondary structure, in vitro digestion kinetics, and predicted standardized ileal amino acid digestibility in broiler chickens.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the chemical composition, protein secondary structure, crude protein (CP) solubilization, and in-vitro amino acid (AA) digestibility of three Kenyan full-fat soybean (FFSB) samples (S1, S2, S3) with unknown processing histories and compared with Canadian samples: raw FFSB, extruded FFSB at 160.0 °C, and FFSB roasted at 136.7 °C, 151.7 °C, or 154.4 °C. Protein structure was characterized using attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. A two-phase in-vitro digestion model was used to determine CP solubilization and AA digestibility. Observed in-vi
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study shows that the origin and thermal processing history of full-fat soybeans strongly influence protein secondary structure, which in turn affects in vitro protein solubilization and amino acid digestion kinetics. Kenyan samples with unknown processing histories were compared to Canadian soybeans subjected to defined extrusion and roasting temperatures, revealing that processing conditions and source both shape predicted standardized ileal amino acid digestibility for broiler chickens. The work highlights FTIR-based protein structure analysis as a useful predictor of nutritional quality in feed ingredients.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences with extensive coverage of UniProtKB and mappings to resources like Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central resource for functional annotation of protein sequences.

papers.title: Machine learning-guided dual optimization of the substrate specificity and thermostability of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase.
papers.abstract: Yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I (YADH) catalyzes the reversible reduction of aldehydes to primary alcohols. Thermostable YADH variants with broad substrate specificities at elevated temperatures are desirable for industrial biocatalysis. In this study, we aimed to alter the substrate specificity of YADH to efficiently catalyze the reduction of the non-native substrate, trans-2-nonenal, to trans-2-nonenol, while simultaneously enhancing thermostability. Residues around the substrate-binding site were identified by docking simulation and subjected to saturation and random mutagenesis. Measured act
papers.summary: This study used machine learning to guide protein engineering of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I, combining docking-based identification of substrate-binding site residues with saturation and random mutagenesis. The goal was to simultaneously broaden substrate specificity toward the non-native substrate trans-2-nonenal and improve thermostability, yielding variants suited for industrial biocatalysis at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Exploration of vetiver-derived compounds for addressing remedy against male infertility using in silco approach.
papers.abstract: The rising prevalence of reproductive disorders, including male infertility, necessitates innovative therapeutic strategies. Plant-based extracts, particularly those from Chrysopogon zizanioides (vetiver plant), have emerged as promising candidates. This study employs in silico methodologies to evaluate the therapeutic potential of vetiver-derived compounds against male infertility. This research aims to investigate the pharmacokinetic profiles, bioactivity, toxicity, and molecular interactions of vetiver compounds with proteins implicated in male reproductive health.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) methods to screen compounds derived from the vetiver plant (Chrysopogon zizanioides) for potential activity against proteins linked to male infertility. The authors assess pharmacokinetics, bioactivity, toxicity, and molecular docking interactions, aiming to identify plant-based candidates for treating reproductive disorders. The work is preliminary and relies entirely on computational predictions without experimental validation.

papers.title: Phytochemical Screening, Pharmacological Evaluation, and Exploratory In Silico Analysis of Emilia sonchifolia Extract and Solvent Fractions.
papers.abstract: Emilia sonchifolia (L.) DC. is a medicinal plant used traditionally for the management of several disorders; however, integrated experimental evaluation of its pharmacological properties remains limited. This study evaluated the phytochemical composition and selected biological activities of the methanolic whole-plant extract of E. sonchifolia (MEES) and its solvent-partitioned fractions and explored possible molecular interactions of literature-reported pyrrolizidine alkaloids using computational approaches. Qualitative phytochemical screening, brine shrimp lethality, 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhyd
papers.summary: This study screened the methanolic extract of Emilia sonchifolia and its solvent fractions for phytochemical content and biological activities, including brine shrimp lethality and antioxidant assays, and used computational docking to explore interactions of reported pyrrolizidine alkaloids with molecular targets. The work provides an integrated experimental and in silico characterization of a traditionally used medicinal plant, though the findings are preliminary and largely descriptive.

papers.title: A Scalable, Traceable Computational-to-Experimental Pipeline for Activity-Guided Identification of Bioactive Constituents: A Case Study in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge.
papers.abstract: Systematic identification of bioactive constituents from complex natural products remains challenging. Here, a scalable and traceable integrated workflow was developed and validated in Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (SMB) for anti-Parkinson's disease (PD) constituent discovery. Network pharmacology first identified four candidate compounds, which were quantified and dynamically tracked during X-5 macroporous resin enrichment and fractionation using a validated HPLC method. Transfer rates exceeded 80% for all candidates, confirming efficient enrichment and chemical traceability. Bioactivity was then
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated computational-to-experimental workflow for identifying bioactive compounds from the medicinal plant Salvia miltiorrhiza, targeting Parkinson's disease. Network pharmacology prioritized four candidate compounds, which were then tracked through enrichment and fractionation steps using a validated HPLC method, with transfer rates above 80% confirming efficient and traceable processing. The approach demonstrates a scalable strategy for linking computational predictions to experimentally verified bioactive constituents in complex natural products.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: This study uses cryo-EM to determine the high-resolution structure of podophage A1002, a virus that infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The authors identify 11 structural proteins and describe a novel split-nozzle tail architecture with two-protein chain-like fibers, providing a structural template for engineering phage-based antimicrobials against this major pathogen.

papers.title: Aptamers without SELEX: De novo design from protein structure in hours.
papers.abstract: Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX)-based aptamer discovery can be constrained by target availability, selection biases, and optimization requirements. We introduce Xelari, a modular pipeline for de novo DNA and RNA aptamer design from protein structures without target-specific SELEX data or retraining. Xelari combines algorithmic modules with surrogate models trained on physical or structural references. InNA reproduced nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies with RMSE of 0.19 kcal/mol across 483,735 reference pairs. AliNA achieved a mean F1 of 0.757 on 339 PD
papers.summary: The authors present Xelari, a modular computational pipeline that designs DNA and RNA aptamers de novo directly from protein structures, bypassing experimental SELEX selection. It combines algorithmic modules with surrogate models trained on physical or structural references, reproducing nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies with low error and achieving reasonable interaction-prediction performance. This offers a rapid, target-agnostic route to aptamer discovery in hours rather than weeks.

papers.title: Clonal tree frequency analysis reveals affinity determinants and enables antibody lead optimization.
papers.abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. We identified M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity-governing mutations, corroborated by AlphaFold2 structural modeling and molecular dynamics free‑energy decomposition. The I33/I100 genotype predicted significantly improved functional neutralization o
papers.summary: This study applies amino acid frequency analysis across a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 antibodies to identify mutations that govern binding affinity. The authors pinpoint M33I and L100I in the heavy chain as key affinity determinants, supported by AlphaFold2 modeling and molecular dynamics free-energy decomposition, and show the I33/I100 genotype predicts improved functional neutralization. The approach offers a practical framework for antibody lead optimization.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied to study and target BMP4, a TGF-β family signaling protein implicated in development, cancer, fibrosis, and the rare bone disease FOP. It covers AI-driven structure prediction, drug discovery efforts, and clinical translation, arguing that these methods open new avenues for understanding BMP4 biology across scales. As a review, it synthesizes recent progress rather than presenting new experimental data.

papers.title: Prediction of the binding modes between key differential flavor compounds in tobacco leaves at different maturity stages and the olfactory receptor OR1D2.
papers.abstract: Leaf maturity is a critical determinant of the sensory quality of tobacco. To elucidate the microstructural characteristics of Yunyan 87 tobacco at distinct maturity stages and the perception mechanisms of key differential flavor compounds mediated by the olfactory receptor OR1D2.
papers.summary: This study examines how tobacco leaf maturity affects flavor compound profiles and predicts how key differential flavor compounds bind to the human olfactory receptor OR1D2. It combines chemical profiling of Yunyan 87 leaves at different maturity stages with molecular docking/modeling of compound–receptor interactions. The work links agricultural maturity to sensory perception mechanisms at the receptor level.

papers.title: Loop region mutations in Omp33-36: unveiling reduced antimicrobial permeability and resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii through structural modeling and membrane-protein simulations.
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii can reduce its susceptibility to antimicrobials by altering the permeability of the outer membrane, e.g., by changing the abundance and function of porins. Omp33-36 has been implicated in susceptibility to multiple antibiotics including carbapenems, but the structural effect of sequence variations observed in clinical isolates is poorly understood. We investigated whether substitutions in Omp33-36 from multidrug-resistant clinical isolates affect porin dynamics and contribute to permeability-related resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and membrane-protein simulations to investigate how mutations in the loop regions of the Acinetobacter baumannii porin Omp33-36 affect its dynamics and membrane permeability. The authors link sequence variants from multidrug-resistant clinical isolates to altered porin behavior that may reduce antimicrobial uptake, offering a structural explanation for permeability-based resistance.

papers.title: Integrated computational screening and biochemical validation identify natural small molecules targeting Aβ aggregation and dissociation.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ), a pathological hallmark implicated in disease onset and progression. Aβ undergoes self-assembly from monomers into soluble oligomers, protofibrils, insoluble fibrils, and extracellular plaques. Our previous studies have shown that Jowiseungchungtang, which consists of 14 medicinal herbs, inhibits Aβ aggregation and ameliorates Aβ-mediated pathology in AD models. However, the active small molecules underlying these effects remain unidentified. To identify small molecules from these 14 medicinal herbs, we constructe
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques
papers.summary: This study combines computational screening with biochemical experiments to identify natural small molecules from a 14-herb traditional medicine (Jowiseungchungtang) that can both inhibit amyloid-beta aggregation and dissociate existing aggregates. The work links specific phytochemicals to the anti-amyloid effects previously observed for the herbal formula, providing a molecular rationale for its use in Alzheimer's disease models.

papers.title: Cannabidiol suppresses M2-like macrophage polarization via TRPV4/RhoA/ROCK signaling to alleviate hepatic fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated buildup of extracellular matrix constitutes a hallmark of hepatic fibrosis, loss of liver architectural integrity, and impaired hepatic functional capacity. Pro-fibrogenic M2-polarized macrophages promote the transdifferentiation of hepatic stellate cells and facilitate fibrotic progression. Cannabidiol (CBD) exhibits immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic properties. However, whether CBD regulates M2-like macrophage polarization to mitigate hepatic fibrogenesis remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether cannabidiol (CBD) can reduce liver fibrosis by preventing macrophages from adopting a pro-fibrotic M2-like state. The authors propose that CBD acts through TRPV4/RhoA/ROCK signaling to suppress M2-like macrophage polarization, thereby limiting hepatic stellate cell activation and fibrotic progression. The work identifies a specific molecular pathway linking CBD's immunomodulatory effects to anti-fibrotic outcomes in the liver.

papers.title: Mechanistic investigation of clarithromycin in ulcerative colitis involving Kv1.3 downregulation and modulation of the Th17/Treg balance.
papers.abstract: Present therapies for ulcerative colitis (UC) frequently encounter challenges due to medication resistance and side effects, underscoring the necessity to discover secure and efficacious therapeutic targets. Clarithromycin (CLA), a macrolide antibiotic, has not been fully characterized with respect to its anti-inflammatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential in UC.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether clarithromycin, a macrolide antibiotic, can alleviate ulcerative colitis by downregulating the potassium channel Kv1.3 and rebalancing Th17 and regulatory T cells. The findings suggest a mechanistic rationale for repurposing clarithromycin as an anti-inflammatory therapy in UC, though the abstract only outlines the investigative approach rather than reporting specific results.

papers.title: The Plant-Derived Peptide Hyde C1 Exhibits Membrane-Associated Antifungal Activity and Protects Against Systemic Candida albicans Infection.
papers.abstract: Invasive candidiasis and increasing antifungal resistance underscore the need for alternative therapeutic approaches. Antimicrobial peptides are of interest because of their antifungal activity and potential membrane-associated effects. This study evaluated Hyde C1, a plant-derived antimicrobial peptide from Cichorium intybus, for antifungal activity against Candida albicans and examined whether its effects were associated with fungal membrane-associated effects.
papers.summary: This study evaluates Hyde C1, an antimicrobial peptide derived from chicory (Cichorium intybus), for activity against the fungal pathogen Candida albicans. The authors report that the peptide shows antifungal activity that appears to involve membrane-associated effects, and that it protects against systemic C. albicans infection in a model system. The work suggests plant-derived peptides as a possible alternative strategy against invasive candidiasis and antifungal resistance.

papers.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer: knowledge mapping and emerging trends based on a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the global publication landscape, collaboration patterns, thematic structure, and emerging research activity in the literature on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and cancer.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape on PFAS and cancer, identifying publication trends, collaboration networks, and emerging thematic areas. It provides a systematic overview of the field's structure and highlights where research activity is growing, though it does not present new experimental findings.

papers.title: Quercetin attenuates acute inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage: transcriptomics-informed network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) induces secondary brain injury characterized by neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Quercetin (QR), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has shown neuroprotective potential; however, the molecular signatures associated with its effects in acute ICH remain incompletely defined. In this study, QR-related target prediction, ICH-associated gene mining, endoplasmic reticulum stress-related gene annotation, and 2 mouse brain transcriptomic datasets were integra
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, transcriptomic datasets, and experimental validation to show that quercetin reduces acute neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage in mice. The authors identify candidate molecular targets and pathways, then confirm that quercetin treatment attenuates inflammatory and ECM-related gene signatures and improves outcomes in an ICH model.

papers.title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in exacerbating pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and machine learning to predict molecular links between the dietary furan 5-HMF and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, then tests those predictions experimentally. It suggests 5-HMF may exacerbate IPF through shared targets and pathways, though the evidence is largely computational with limited experimental validation.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer and tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways. Using a diabetic-mimetic CRC model, the authors show that hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and alters macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic axis at the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors truncated the HMGB1 B-box peptide (mB Box-97) to identify shorter variants that retain anti-biofilm activity while suppressing NETosis via PKC inhibition. They found that anti-NETotic and anti-biofilm functions can be uncoupled into distinct peptide regions, enabling separation of these activities. This structure-guided minimization could support development of peptide therapeutics with reduced off-target inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review surveys recent protein engineering advances aimed at improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) for industrial use. It focuses on how structure- and sequence-guided engineering strategies address limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, restricted operational adaptability, and product inhibition across biorefinery, food/feed, textile, and pulp applications.
